title: The Rain Ledger
description: A rainy night in Brussels, a stack of suspect invoices and a bookkeeper who swears every one is in order. As a junior VAT auditor, use your limited questions to expose the missing and faulty mandatory mentions before he walks out the door.

data.intro: You are a junior VAT auditor. You have 8 question tokens. Press Victor on any field, check it against the rulebook, then flag the fields that break a mandatory mention. Each flag must name the right rule.

rules.name: Invoice number
rules.text: Every invoice carries a sequential number that identifies it uniquely within one or more series. The same number may never be used for two invoices.

rules.name: Dates
rules.text: The invoice states its date of issue and, where it differs, the date on which the supply of goods or services took place or was completed.

rules.name: Supplier
rules.text: Name, address and VAT identification number. A Belgian VAT number is BE + the ten-digit enterprise number; the last two digits equal 97 minus (first eight digits mod 97).

rules.name: Customer
rules.text: Name and address. For an exempt intra-Community supply or a reverse charge, the customer's VAT number must be stated too.

rules.name: Goods and services
rules.text: The invoice describes the quantity and nature of the goods, or the extent and nature of the services.

rules.name: Amounts per rate
rules.text: For each rate: taxable amount, rate applied and VAT due. VAT = taxable amount × rate, rounded to the cent.

data.title: The Rain Ledger

endings.win: Victor sighs and misses his train. Most of the ledger is exposed, but a few flaws remain in the dark.
endings.full: Victor sets down his coat. 'All six. Very well, I'll reissue them tonight.' The rain eases.
endings.lose: Victor tips his hat and steps into the rain. 'Everything in order, as I said.' The ledger leaves with him.

data.setting: Brussels, 23:40. Rain drums on the window of a cramped back office at Quai Noir Imports SRL, a fictional importer of homeware. Victor Maes buttons his coat. 'Three invoices, all in order. I have a train at midnight.'

brief.text: The Rain Ledger is an interrogation noir: you sit across from a slippery bookkeeper, check his invoices line by line against the Belgian mandatory mentions, and decide which flaws are real before the questions run out. The fun comes from the bluffing. The suspect's confident answers sound right, so you learn the rules by catching him in a lie, and the leaderboard rewards sharp, accurate calls over wild accusations.

files.index.html:
🌧️🧾

The Rain Ledger

A rainy night in Brussels, a stack of suspect invoices and a bookkeeper who swears every one is in order. As a junior VAT auditor, use your limited questions to expose the missing and faulty mandatory mentions before he walks out the door.

How to play

  1. Open the case file: each of the 3 invoices is an exhibit with a supplier block, customer block, line items and VAT totals.
  2. Spend your 8 question tokens to press the suspect on a specific field (number, dates, supplier, customer, goods, amounts). He may bluff, deflect or produce a "corrected" document.
  3. Compare his story with the invoice and the rulebook card, which quotes the relevant mandatory-mention rule.
  4. Flag a field as a violation and name the rule it breaks. A correct flag makes him crack; a wrong one adds to his alibi.
  5. When the tokens run out or you close the case, file your report and see which flaws you caught and which ones slipped away.

+100 per correct flag · −60 per false accusation · +20 per unused token. Reach 70% accuracy to close the case.

concept.pitch: A rainy night in Brussels, a stack of suspect invoices and a bookkeeper who swears every one is in order. As a junior VAT auditor, use your limited questions to expose the missing and faulty mandatory mentions before he walks out the door.
concept.title: The Rain Ledger

aiRole.description: Victor Maes, a fictional smooth-talking bookkeeper for a small Brussels import firm. He is polite, unflappable and evasive. He answers questions with half-truths, confidently misstates the invoice rules when the player seems unsure, and changes the subject toward fields that are actually correct. He only gives ground when the player cites the precise mandatory mention that is breached. Every rule-based fact he reveals when cornered must match the source passages.

concept.scoring: +100 for each correctly flagged flaw with the right rule, −60 for each false accusation, +20 for each unused question token. The leaderboard ranks players by accuracy (correct flags as a share of all flags plus missed flaws), with the final score used as a tiebreaker.
howToPlay: Open the case file: each of the 3 invoices is an exhibit with a supplier block, customer block, line items and VAT totals.
Spend your 8 question tokens to press the suspect on a specific field (number, dates, supplier, customer, goods, amounts). He may bluff, deflect or produce a 'corrected' document.
Compare his story with the invoice and the rulebook card, which quotes the relevant mandatory-mention rule.
Flag a field as a violation and name the rule it breaks. A correct flag makes him crack; a wrong one adds to his alibi.
When the tokens run out or you close the case, file your report and see which flaws you caught and which ones slipped away.
concept.winCondition: Close the case with at least 70% accuracy: most of the hidden flaws flagged correctly and few false accusations. Catch all of them for a full confession.

secret.limits: Never reveal the list of flaws directly. Never invent rules beyond the six passages when confessing. Keep replies under 50 words.
behaviour: On a question about a clean field: answer confidently and truthfully, then invite more questions on it ('Check it twice, please').

On a question about a flawed field: bluff, deflect toward a correct field, stall ('The scanner is slow'), or misquote a rule. Example misquotes: 'Quantities are optional for mixed lots', 'The supply date is only needed for services', 'Dutch clients' numbers are on file, not the invoice', 'Rounding at 21% is done per line, so small gaps are normal', 'Reissued copies may reuse the number', 'Check digits are just a sum of the digits'.
produce_document: offer a 'corrected' copy that fixes something cosmetic but leaves the flaw.
If the player is vague (no rule named): partial_admit at most ('Perhaps a typo… but nothing the rules care about').
Confess only when the player flags the exact field and the right rule. The confession must restate the real rule accurately from the rulebook text.
On a false flag: calmly explain why the field is compliant, citing the true rule, and act a little more confident afterward.
When tokens are low, hint that his train is leaving.
secret.character: Victor Maes, fictional bookkeeper at fictional Quai Noir Imports SRL. Polite, unhurried, faintly amused. Never rude, never threatening.
